validated_results.title: Correlations between meteorological parameters and prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: This county-level ecological analysis examined meteorological parameters (temperature, humidity, snowfall, pesticide proxies) and only mentions low vitamin D as a competing hypothesis, providing no measured vitamin D exposure estimate.

validated_results.title: A large prospective study of SEP15 genetic variation, interaction with plasma selenium levels, and prostate cancer risk and survival.
validated_results.reason: The report centers on a genotype-stratified or gene-exposure interaction, which this protocol excludes.

validated_results.title: Is prostate cancer prevention with selenium all in the genes?
validated_results.reason: This is a perspective/commentary discussing another group's findings and contains no original study results.

validated_results.title: Plasma phytanic acid concentration and risk of prostate cancer: results from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
validated_results.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
validated_results.reason: The measured exposure is plasma phytanic acid concentration, a distinct fatty-acid biomarker, and no dairy intake estimate for prostate cancer risk is reported.

validated_results.title: [Selenium in complementary oncology. A critical comments on the SELECT trial].
validated_results.reason: The record is a critical commentary on the SELECT trial without original comparative results.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in inflammatory genes, plasma antioxidants, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Reported estimates are COX-2 and IL-8 genotype effects stratified by plasma antioxidant levels rather than a population-wide antioxidant effect on prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in inflammatory genes, plasma antioxidants, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: The beta-carotene results are presented only as genotype-stratified odds ratios for inflammatory gene variants, with no population-wide beta-carotene estimate.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in inflammatory genes, plasma antioxidants, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Lutein/zeaxanthin appears only as a stratifying variable in gene-antioxidant interaction analyses without a population-wide lutein risk estimate.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in inflammatory genes, plasma antioxidants, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Plasma lycopene is used only to stratify the COX-2 polymorphism effect, so no population-wide lycopene-prostate cancer estimate is available.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in inflammatory genes, plasma antioxidants, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Plasma selenium is reported only as an effect modifier of the COX-2 variant rather than as an independent exposure for prostate cancer risk.

validated_results.title: Polymorphisms in inflammatory genes, plasma antioxidants, and prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Zeaxanthin is only part of a genotype-stratified interaction analysis (as lutein/zeaxanthin) with no population-wide exposure estimate.

validated_results.title: Meta-analysis of observational studies of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels and colorectal, breast and prostate cancer and colorectal adenoma.
validated_results.reason: This is a systematic review with meta-analysis of observational studies of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and cancer, not an original human study.
